ai_view.directive: Follow as written. Merge statistical knowledge freely; merge operational baselines carefully; never merge certification merely because two scopes behave similarly. Separate three operations that are easily confused: statistical pooling (share information to improve estimates; requires verified comparability, calibrated uncertainty, independence assumptions), operational baseline merge (share a forecasting/alert model; requires independent evidence that shared modeling preserves each scope's detection quality), qualification consolidation (one certification covering several scopes; requires proof the guarantee covers every member and relevant cross-scope interactions). A statistically pooled group must never automatically become one certified operating scope.

intelligence.essence: Evidence-Preserving Scope Evolution Law: NayaNET may merge statistical estimation across demonstrably comparable scopes and split models when independently established semantic or behavioral differences warrant it. Every observation retains its original provenance, and every provider guarantee remains bound to its independently demonstrated applicability. Statistical pooling shall never create, broaden, inherit or restore qualification or execution authority. Similarity permits information sharing. Demonstrated coverage permits qualification. Statistical similarity alone never grants authority or extends a provider guarantee into an untested scope. The operating standard: 'Endpoint B has little data, so I will borrow statistical knowledge from comparable Endpoint A. But I will not borrow A's proof. If B develops a regression, I will detect it separately. If a new workload appears, I will give it a provisional model and qualify only the guarantees that actually cover it.' That is how NayaNET becomes statistically smarter without becoming epistemically less trustworthy.
intelligence.falsifier: A shared model that automatically becomes a shared certification; a sparse endpoint inheriting an idempotency certificate by resemblance; 'no significant difference found' treated as proof of equivalence (especially with 15 vs 10,000 observations); rewritten historical observations under a new taxonomy; silent reallocation of ambiguous records; a merge racing an incident withdrawal; an unresolved incident's training data treated as healthy evidence; a new workload qualified by a shared statistical parent's contract coverage.

human_view.meaning: Three things that look alike but aren't: sharing math to get better estimates, sharing one forecasting model, and sharing one certificate. The law keeps them separate forever. Every observation keeps its original identity — where it came from, which guarantee actually covers it, where estimates were borrowed from, where cross-boundary effects were tested — four separate labels, so organizing intelligence efficiently never erases where it came from. Four decisions for four situations: borrow estimates for sparse-but-comparable scopes, merge the model only with proof each member still detects its own failures, split when meaning or behavior genuinely differs, and give every new workload a provisional home that borrows forecasts but inherits no certificates. The standing warning: failing to find a difference is not finding equivalence — fifteen observations that 'look like' ten thousand proven ones earn better estimates, never a certificate. New workload classes walk a four-step path from registered to provisionally modeled to independently qualified to qualified-in-scope — and a genuinely general provider contract can cover a new workload, but only after verifying every condition actually applies. Every merge or split is a versioned, reconstructable record that never rewrites history and never races an incident. Ten adversarial tests, crowned by swapping in the defective assumption 'shared model implies shared qualification' and watching the checker catch the sparse endpoint stealing the certificate — then restoring the guard and confirming useful learning survives while the theft stays blocked.

Permanent contributions: the three-operation separation (pooling ≠ model merge ≠ qualification consolidation), the four scope-identity IDs (statistical_parent, qualification_scope, observation_scope, interaction_scope), the four scope decisions, the four comparability conditions, the 'absence of detected difference ≠ equivalence' principle with its equivalence-margin requirement, the semantic-vs-statistical split criteria, the provisional-scope lifecycle, the no-qualification-transfer invariant (UseGuarantee ⇒ Verified ∧ in-scope ∧ Current ∧ LAWValid), versioned reconstructable change records, and the M1–M10 suite with the guard-swap mutation. Shawn's explicit scoping stands: isolated test mechanism first, never an unreviewed production authority change.

naya_view.directive: Never confuse pooling estimates with merging models with consolidating qualification. Keep the four scope identities distinct on every observation. Pool only on demonstrated comparability with calibrated uncertainty; merge models only with per-member detection proof; consolidate qualification only with full-union coverage proof. Split on semantic difference immediately, on statistical divergence when independently established — never on sparse-sample noise, never requiring significance to separate different safety contracts. Register new workloads as provisional scopes; qualify only guarantees whose actual conditions are verified. Version every change; never rewrite provenance; never race incidents. Test with M1–M10 and the guard-swap mutation.

simple_view.meaning: Borrow the math, never the proof — scopes may share estimates but certificates stay with the evidence that earned them.
